paragraphs.source_en: Around the Hour of the Serpent, the daimyos assembled at Daitokuji formed an orderly procession and passed before the watching crowds, their splendid train lending still greater majesty and grandeur to the funeral. Most striking of all, naturally, was the coffin draped in golden gauze and silk. The jeweled pendants hanging on all four sides and the railings were inlaid throughout with gold and silver; the octagonal pillars were covered in gorgeous paintings, and beneath the sunlight their dazzling colors cast out rainbow after seven-colored rainbow. Inside the coffin, of course, rested the figure carved from aloeswood of which Hideyoshi was so proud.
